candidate: domain-separated deterministic claim identity from canonical operation schema plus payload hash
tested_scope: Two semantically distinct predecessor role-local payloads that intentionally share the same naive operation label state_write; claim identity is the canonical schema tuple itself, including schema version, role, assignment, operation and payload_sha256. Restart replay is evaluated by exact deterministic tuple reconstruction and exact payload-hash match; no concurrency or adversarial cryptographic collision claim is made.

probe_assertions.restart_reconstruction_rule: Reconstruct the same canonical tuple from role, assignment, operation and stored payload_sha256. Exact tuple equality reproduces the identical claim_id without external stateful compute.
probe_assertions.replay_rule: If exact claim_id exists and stored payload_sha256 equals the reconstructed payload_sha256, return reuse_no_write. If the same operation label has a different payload_sha256, it necessarily selects a different claim_id and must not overwrite the first record.

revision: A naive operation label is not an idempotency key. The claim identity must bind an explicit schema/domain, role/task namespace and exact payload identity; then semantically distinct payload hashes cannot alias merely because the operation label is reused. Replay authorization remains exact-match only.

mechanism_assessment.repository_transport_role: bounded role-local create/read transport only; no hosted compute or scheduler mutation
mechanism_assessment.accepted_scope: claim identity derivation and exact-match restart replay for two distinct payload hashes under one operation label

limits_and_unresolved_child: This does not yet prove canonical payload serialization across byte-different but semantically equivalent encodings or safe schema evolution. Next test must normalize equivalent JSON forms and explicit schema versions before hashing/claim derivation, while preserving distinct identities for genuinely different payload semantics.
